subject: Chemistry
question: Estimate the enthalpy change for 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g) using the bond enthalpies H–H 436, O=O 498 and O–H 463 kJ mol⁻¹.
response_text:
2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g)

Bonds broken: 2 × (H–H) + 1 × (O=O) = 2(436) + 498 = 1370 kJ mol⁻¹
Bonds formed: 4 × (O–H) = 4(463) = 1852 kJ mol⁻¹
ΔH = 1370 − 1852 = −482 kJ mol⁻¹

The reaction is exothermic because more energy is released when the O–H bonds form than is needed to break the H–H and O=O bonds.
